transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-19 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Maya Chen, Rajiv Shah, Elena Park (Redwood) — Laura Mendes, Tom Alvarez, Priya Kapoor, Samir Patel (Cobalt CU)
Recording: auto-generated Fireflies transcript (medium quality)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on audit readiness, key management (KMS/HSM), and where logs and telemetry would land across Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployments. Customer cares about: legal hold, retention windows, redaction, and third-party access.

Topics covered:
- Audit evidence and which artifacts Redwood can provide (SOC2, ISO references, deployment evidence)
- Key residency and KMS/HSM integration options (customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed)
- Log collection, retention, and redaction strategies for GDPR/HIPAA/FFIEC-style audits
- Deployment tradeoffs: Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private VPC/on-prem
- Timeline, stakeholders, and next steps for a pilot

Shared artifacts mentioned:
- link: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-summary (SOC2 summary)
- link: https://redwood.example.com/docs/kms-integration (KMS integration diagram)
- link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/benchmarks-redwood-cobalt (performance spreadsheet - access pending)

Action items (recap in call):
- See action_items metadata above; all agreed on owners and rough due dates.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we have about 50 minutes. quick intros?
[00:06] Laura Mendes: Hi, Laura here, head of cloud and security at Cobalt Credit Union. we've been evaluating a few inference platforms; we're most worried about audit artifacts and key residency.
[00:12] Maya Chen: Great. Rajiv, want to intro from the technical side?
[00:16] Rajiv Shah: Sure. I'm Rajiv, I do solutions for Redwood, focus on private and dedicated deployments. we'll go through options and what evidence we can hand you for audits.
[00:24] Tom Alvarez: Quick thing — we run a mix of on-prem and GCP. our legal team wants to know if keys can stay inside our HSMs, and how logs are stored, like raw prompts vs obfuscated.
[00:34] Rajiv Shah: Totally, that's a common ask. We support customer-managed K-M-S — sorry, KMS — integrations. For Private you can use your HSM or KMS and we can ensure the control plane doesn't have plaintext access to keys. For Dedicated, we do a bring-your-key model with envelope encryption.
[00:50] Laura Mendes: When you say "control plane doesn't have access" — do you provide attestation or evidence?
[00:56] Rajiv Shah: We can provide attestation reports and deployment manifests, and for Private deployments we can supply runbook-level evidence of key operations. The SOC2 package covers many of the controls; we also have additional logs that show key rotation events.
[01:10] Priya Kapoor: We need explicit audit trails for any access to unredacted data. HIPAA-wise, even metadata access can be sensitive. Does Redwood store the full transcript logs in hosted mode by default?
[01:22] Maya Chen: By default, hosted captures request/response logs for debugging and billing, but we have opt-out and retention controls. For healthcare or finance we recommend Dedicated or Private with log forwarding to your SIEM and stricter retention.
[01:36] Tom Alvarez: How flexible is the log redaction? we can't have account numbers crossing into logs.
[01:41] Rajiv Shah: We have configurable redaction at ingest and at rest. There's an automatic PII heuristic and you can plug in custom regex filters. Caveat: heuristics are not 100% perfect, so for regulated PII we often pair redaction with a prefix-cache plus local tokenization in your VPC for Private deployments.
[01:59] Laura Mendes: If we do Private, will Redwood's Console still be able to show per-route latency metrics? We need that for ops.
[02:06] Elena Park: Yes, telemetry can be exposed via a metrics endpoint that you own. In Private, the telemetry collectors can push to your monitoring stack; we can also offer read-only snapshots for Redwood support under a strict access policy.
[02:20] Samir Patel: What's the typical evidence set you hand over during an audit?
[02:24] Rajiv Shah: We provide SOC2 report, architecture diagrams, deployment manifests, key rotation logs, access logs (RBAC events), and if needed, a detailed operational playbook. Some customers also ask for packet-level evidence — that's tougher and we usually recommend a joint-attestation approach.
[02:39] Priya Kapoor: About legal hold: if we need to place a legal hold on a user or account, can we preserve raw prompts and outputs? or does your retention policy auto-prune?
[02:49] Rajiv Shah: We can create a legal-hold retention bucket where items are immutable for the hold duration. That is easier to set up in Dedicated/Private. Hosted allows custom retention windows but legal-hold immutability is best done with a private object store under your control.
[03:03] Tom Alvarez: Any concerns about cross-border backups? we have EU members and we need data residency in EEA.
[03:09] Maya Chen: We support region-locking. For Hosted, you can pick region and we provide EEA-only storage options. For Dedicated and Private, you physically choose the cluster region; backups can be configured to stay inside the region, and we support geo-fencing for failover if required.
[03:24] Laura Mendes: On KMS: we use AWS CloudHSM in a single-tenant mode. Can Redwood call our CloudHSM for key operations without seeing plaintext?
[03:32] Rajiv Shah: Yes, with envelope encryption. The signing/decryption happens in your CloudHSM; Redwood only gets wrapped keys. For mutual TLS and attestation we can do a small PoC to validate the handshake.
[03:42] Priya Kapoor: Are audit logs tamper-evident? we need chain-of-custody for FFIEC and state regulators.
[03:48] Rajiv Shah: We can produce append-only audit logs with checksums and optional streaming into your WORM (write once read many) archive. For private setups it's straightforward; for hosted we can forward logs to your S3 retention bucket with immutability flags.
[04:02] Tom Alvarez: How about encryption-in-use concerns — you mentioned KV cache earlier, is that encrypted?
[04:08] Rajiv Shah: The KV cache (we sometimes say K-V cache) is encrypted at rest and in-memory is guarded by OS-level protections. If you need in-use encryption we recommend Private with enclave-based options — that's a more advanced add-on and we'd evaluate performance tradeoffs.
[04:23] Samir Patel: Performance — if we pin a model and run canaries for latency, what's the typical overhead of envelope encryption?
[04:30] Rajiv Shah: Envelope adds a small constant overhead on initial request to unwrap keys (tens to low hundreds of ms depending on HSM latency). After that, token-serving is unaffected; we keep a KV cache for wrapped keys so steady-state is fine. Our benchmarking sheet will show samples.
[04:45] Laura Mendes: For HIPAA, is the business associate agreement standard?
[04:48] Maya Chen: We have a BAA template and we sign BAAs for customers with covered workloads. We'll send the legal team the standard BAA and we can discuss modifications.
[04:57] Priya Kapoor: A couple of nitty-gritty items: can we restrict Redwood support to read-only access to logs and require two-person approval for key rotation?
[05:05] Elena Park: Yes — tunable RBAC. We can require dual-approval workflows for sensitive operations, and we log approvals into the audit trail.
[05:13] Tom Alvarez: What's the rollback plan if an upgrade changes output quality? regulators will ask for evidence that we tested.
[05:20] Rajiv Shah: We support canary rollouts and automated rollback policies in the rollout config. We also store eval run results tied to prompt sets so you can show pre/post quality checks.
[05:31] Priya Kapoor: Do you support data minimization at the route level? for some endpoints we only want embeddings and no full text retained.
[05:38] Rajiv Shah: Route-level policies are supported. You can configure per-route retention and choose to only store embeddings or hashed fingerprints while dropping the text.
[05:46] Laura Mendes: Can you show an example of evidence you gave another credit union?
[05:50] Maya Chen: We can't share customer-specific artifacts, but we can provide a redacted evidence bundle and a template runbook. We'll attach that with the SOC2 summary.
[05:59] Samir Patel: On timeline — if we like Dedicated, how long to stand up a proof-of-concept?
[06:03] Rajiv Shah: Typically 2–4 weeks for a Dedicated PoC: provisioning, VPC peering, KMS integration, and a small routing policy setup. Private takes longer depending on your on-prem readiness.
[06:14] Tom Alvarez: Costs — I'd like a TCO estimate for Dedicated vs Private including HSM egress costs.
[06:18] Rajiv Shah: We'll do that. We'll need your estimated QPS and model size; you mentioned 200 RPS earlier — we'll use that as a starting point.
[06:26] Laura Mendes: What about third party subpoenas — will Redwood ever be compelled to share?
[06:30] Maya Chen: As a provider, Redwood responds to valid legal process in accordance with law and contract. For Private deployments under your control, Redwood would not have access to customer data to produce; for Hosted, we'll work with you and your legal team.
